toc.title: How Tool Results Reach the Model

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; SDK: software development kit

  • The agentic loop lifecycle: request, inspect stop_reason, run the tools, return the results, repeat
  • How tool results are added to the conversation history
  • Model-driven decisions versus pre-configured decision trees or tool sequences
  • The anti-patterns that the exam names: parsing natural language, an iteration cap as the main stop, checking for assistant text

2The Agentic Loop

Running case

Birchwood Supply Answers a Return Request

  • A customer writes: "My blender arrived cracked. I want my money back."
  • The support agent must look up the customer, find the order, check the return policy and issue a refund
  • Nobody knows in advance how many tool calls that takes: the agent decides step by step

An agentic loop lets Claude work toward a goal over several steps. Each cycle has the same shape:

  1. Send a request to Claude with the conversation so far and the list of tools.
  2. Inspect stop_reason in the response.
  3. If it is "tool_use", Claude wants tools run: execute each requested tool in your code.
  4. Append the results to the conversation (the assistant message with the tool_use blocks, then a user message with the matching tool_result blocks) and send the next request.
  5. If it is "end_turn", Claude has finished: stop the loop and present the final answer.

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": user_text}]
while True:
    resp = client.messages.create(model=MODEL, max_tokens=1024,
                                  tools=TOOLS, messages=messages)
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": resp.content})
    if resp.stop_reason == "tool_use":
        results = [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": b.id,
                    "content": run_tool(b.name, b.input)}
                   for b in resp.content if b.type == "tool_use"]
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})   # tool results go back as a user message
    elif resp.stop_reason == "end_turn":
        break                                                    # finished: show resp to the user
Exam tip

The loop continues when stop_reason is "tool_use" and terminates when it is "end_turn". Memorize both values and what each triggers.

3How Tool Results Reach the Model

  • The API is stateless: Claude only knows what you send. After a tool runs, you must append the result to the history so the next request can reason about it.
  • The history grows in pairs: the assistant message (text plus tool_use blocks) and the user message carrying the tool_result blocks, each linked by tool_use_id.
  • Rules of the API: the tool_result blocks must immediately follow the assistant's tool_use message, and in that user message the tool_result blocks must come first, before any text Beyond the guide.
  • Claude may request several tools in one response (parallel tool use): run them all and return all the results in one user message Beyond the guide.
  • If a tool fails, return the error text in the tool_result with is_error: true so Claude can adapt instead of guessing Beyond the guide.

Exam tip

The API is stateless: if a question says Claude "forgot" an earlier tool result, the history was not appended or resent.

4Model-Driven Versus Pre-Configured

Model-driven (agentic loop) Pre-configured (decision tree or fixed sequence)
Who chooses the next tool? Claude, from the context and the last tool results Your code, in a fixed order or rule set
Best for Open-ended tasks where the path depends on what is found Predictable steps with a known order
Risk The model may skip or reorder steps unless something enforces them Rigid; breaks on cases you did not foresee
Exam link This task statement Used with the model-driven loop when order is mandatory (Module 3)
  • The exam contrasts "Claude reasons about which tool to call next based on context" with "pre-configured decision trees or tool sequences". The agentic loop is the first.
  • A fixed order that is required by the business is not solved by turning the whole agent into a decision tree; you add enforcement at the points that matter (Module 3).
Exam tip

"Claude decides the next tool from context" is the agentic (model-driven) pattern; "your code fixes the order" is pre-configured. A required order is enforced at specific points (Module 3), not by dropping the loop.

5Stopping the Loop Correctly

Anti-pattern Why it fails
Parsing natural language ("if the reply says 'I'm done'") Wording varies; a polite sentence can appear while a tool call is still pending
An arbitrary iteration cap as the main stop (for example 5 turns) Cuts off tasks that need more steps and wastes turns on easy ones; the cap hides the real signal
Checking for assistant text as a completion indicator Claude often writes text together with a tool_use block ("Let me look that up")
  • Use stop_reason as the authoritative signal.
  • A maximum-turns or budget limit is still a good safety net against runaway loops; it is just not the primary stopping mechanism Beyond the guide.

Other stop reasons Beyond the guide

stop_reason Meaning What to do
end_turn Claude finished naturally Present the answer
tool_use Claude requests tool calls Run them, append results, continue
max_tokens The reply hit your max_tokens limit The output is cut off: raise the limit or continue the turn
stop_sequence A stop sequence you set was produced Handle as your design requires
pause_turn A server-side tool loop paused Send the response back to continue
refusal Claude declined the request Handle as a refusal, do not retry blindly

[Verify live] The Claude Agent SDK runs this loop for you: it keeps going until Claude replies with no tool calls, then returns a result whose subtype is success; limits such as maxTurns end it with error_max_turns instead. As of 8 November 2026.

6Exam Q&A

S1Birchwood's support agent sometimes stops after Claude writes "Let me check that order for you" even though the same response contains a tool_use block. The loop ends because it checks whether the response contains any text. What is the best fix?

  • AContinue the loop while stop_reason is "tool_use" and stop when it is "end_turn"
  • BStop the loop only after exactly five iterations
  • CSearch the text for the word "done" before stopping
  • DAdd a system prompt line telling Claude never to write any text before it calls a tool, so that text always means done
Show the answer

Answer: A. stop_reason is the authoritative loop signal. Text can accompany a tool call, so text is not a completion indicator; a prompt tweak, a fixed count and a keyword search all keep a fragile signal.

S2A developer ends the agent run after a fixed 8 iterations because "most tasks finish by then". Several complex refund cases return incomplete answers. What is the root problem?

  • AThe tools return so much data that the conversation history overflows
  • BThe model is too small to finish complex refund cases within one run
  • CThe system prompt is too long
  • DAn arbitrary iteration cap is the main stop signal
Show the answer

Answer: D. A cap cuts off tasks that need more steps. Terminate on end_turn; keep a cap only as a safety limit.

S3After running a requested tool, what must the application do before the next request?

  • AStart a new conversation with only the tool result
  • BDiscard the tool output to save tokens and let Claude infer the result from its own earlier reasoning
  • CSend the tool result as a system prompt
  • DAppend the assistant tool_use message and a user message with the matching tool_result to the history
Show the answer

Answer: D. The API is stateless; the model can reason about the result only if it is in the history it receives.

S4Which design uses model-driven decision making?

  • AA lookup table keyed by the customer's account type
  • BA script that always calls search, then summarize, then email in that order
  • CA rule engine that maps keywords in the user message to tools
  • DA loop in which Claude picks the next tool from the context
Show the answer

Answer: D. Model-driven means Claude chooses the next action from context. The other options are pre-configured sequences.

S5Claude returns a response with stop_reason: "tool_use" containing three tool_use blocks. What is the correct handling?

  • ARun all three tools and return all three results in the next user message
  • BReturn an error, because only one tool call is allowed in a single response
  • CWait for the user to choose which tool to run
  • DRun only the first tool and ignore the others
Show the answer

Answer: A. Claude may request several tools at once; run each and return all results together (each linked to its tool_use_id).

S6A team wants protection against runaway loops. Which statement is best?

  • ARemove all limits; stop_reason is enough
  • BUse the iteration cap as the only stop signal
  • CStop whenever the response is longer than 500 words, because long replies mean the task is done
  • DA turn or budget limit as a safety net, with stop_reason as the main signal
Show the answer

Answer: D. A limit is a sensible guard rail, but the loop should normally end on end_turn.

S7A response arrives with stop_reason: "max_tokens" and the answer ends mid-sentence. What does this tell you?

  • AThe reply hit the output limit and was cut off; raise max_tokens
  • BThe user cancelled the request before the model could finish its reply
  • CClaude requested a tool call
  • DClaude finished its task normally and the answer is complete as written
Show the answer

Answer: A. max_tokens means the output limit was reached, so the answer is incomplete.

S8Which TWO statements about the agentic loop are correct? Select TWO.

  • AThe loop ends when the reply contains the word "done"
  • BThe loop continues while stop_reason is "tool_use"
  • CClaude keeps tool results between requests, so the history need not be resent
  • DA fixed iteration count is the recommended primary stop signal
  • ETool results are returned in a user message linked to the request by tool_use_id
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. The loop runs on stop_reason, and results travel back in a user message matched by tool_use_id. Keyword checks and fixed counts are fragile, and the API is stateless so the history must be resent.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Loop Request → inspect stop_reason → run tools → append tool_result → repeat
Continue / stop tool_use = continue, end_turn = stop
History Append the assistant message (with tool_use) and a user message with tool_result blocks, matched by tool_use_id; results come first in that user message
Parallel calls Several tool_use blocks may come at once: run all, return all results together
Model-driven vs fixed Claude chooses next tool from context (agentic) vs your code fixes the order (decision tree)
Anti-patterns Parse text for "done"; arbitrary iteration cap as main stop; treat any text as completion
Safety net A max-turns or budget limit is fine as a guard rail, not as the main stop
Other reasons max_tokens = cut off; refusal = declined; pause_turn = continue; stop_sequence
